question: Which condition, also known as icterus, causes a yellowing of your skin and the whites of your eyes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaundice.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jaundice, also called icterus, is a condition marked by yellowing of the skin, mucous membranes and the whites of the eyes (sclera). (पीलिया / icterus — यकृत से जुड़ा रोग)

 

• It is caused by an excess of bilirubin (a yellow pigment produced from the breakdown of red blood cells) in the blood, usually due to liver dysfunction, bile duct obstruction, or excessive RBC breakdown (haemolysis).

 

• Common causes include hepatitis, cirrhosis, gallstones blocking the bile duct, and certain blood disorders.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Normal serum bilirubin level is about 0.2 to 1.2 mg/dL; jaundice becomes visible when it exceeds roughly 2-3 mg/dL.

 

• Jaundice is broadly classified into pre-hepatic, hepatic, and post-hepatic types depending on where the disruption in bilirubin metabolism occurs.

 

NOTE

 

• Ichthyosis (Option 1): A group of skin disorders causing dry, thickened, scaly skin; unrelated to bilirubin levels.

 

• Eczema (Option 3): A condition causing inflamed, itchy, red skin (dermatitis), not yellowing.

 

• Pemphigus (Option 4): An autoimmune disorder causing blistering of the skin and mucous membranes.

question: Under the leadership of which of the following revolutionaries was Chittagong Armoury Raid conducted?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surya Sen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chittagong Armoury Raid was conducted on the night of 18 April 1930 under the leadership of Surya Sen (Masterda). (चटगांव शस्त्रागार छापा — सूर्य सेन)

 

• The raid was carried out by the Indian Republican Army, Chittagong branch, which raided the police armoury and auxiliary force armoury in Chittagong (now in Bangladesh) to seize arms and disrupt British communication lines.

 

• Prominent associates included Ananta Singh, Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal, Pritilata Waddedar, and Kalpana Dutta.

 

• Surya Sen was eventually captured by the British and executed on 12 January 1934.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pritilata Waddedar led the attack on the Pahartali European Club in 1932 and consumed potassium cyanide to avoid capture.

 

• The raid is also remembered for the phrase "Chittagong Uprising" and inspired later revolutionary activity in Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Rash Behari Bose (Option 1): Associated with the Ghadar Party, the attempted bomb attack on Lord Hardinge (1912), and later the Indian National Army in Southeast Asia.

 

• Badal Gupta (Option 2): One of the three revolutionaries (with Benoy and Dinesh) who attacked Writers' Building, Kolkata in 1930, not the Chittagong raid.

 

• Hemu Kalani (Option 3): A young revolutionary from Sindh executed in 1943 for trying to derail a British military train; unrelated to Chittagong.

question: In which of the following states is Govindji Nartanalaya located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Govindji Nartanalaya is a dance school located at Imphal, Manipur, associated with training in Manipuri classical dance (Ras Lila). (गोविंदजी नर्तनालय — मणिपुर)

 

• It is closely linked to the Shri Govindaji Temple in Imphal, a major centre of Vaishnavite culture in Manipur.

 

• Manipuri dance developed as a devotional art form centred on the Radha-Krishna Ras Lila tradition, and institutions like this nartanalaya were central to preserving and teaching it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manipuri is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, known for its gentle, flowing movements and elaborate costumes (Kumil/Potloi).

 

• The Shri Govindaji Temple in Imphal is one of the most important Vaishnavite shrines in Northeast India.

 

NOTE

 

• Assam (Option 2): Known for Sattriya dance, associated with Vaishnavite sattras (monasteries) founded by Srimanta Sankardev, not Govindji Nartanalaya.

 

• Nagaland (Option 3): Known for tribal folk dances and the Hornbill Festival, not classical Manipuri dance institutions.

 

• Tripura (Option 4): Known for folk dances like Hojagiri, not Govindji Nartanalaya.

question: Which of the following celebrations is dedicated to Sun God and his wife Usha to thank them for sustaining life on earth and for granting wishes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhath Puja.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chhath Puja is a festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and his consort Usha (Chhathi Maiya), celebrated to thank them for sustaining life and for granting wishes and prosperity. (छठ पूजा — सूर्य देव और उषा)

 

• It is primarily observed in Bihar, Jharkhand, and eastern Uttar Pradesh, and involves offering Arghya (water offerings) to the setting and rising sun.

 

• The festival falls on the sixth day (Shashthi) of the Kartik month (Shukla Paksha) in the Hindu calendar, hence the name "Chhath" (meaning "sixth").

 

• Devotees observe a rigorous 36-hour fast without food or water as part of the rituals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chhath Puja is one of the few Hindu festivals where the setting sun is worshipped along with the rising sun, symbolising that one should also have faith during difficult/declining times.

 

• The festival has now spread wherever the Bihari and Purvanchali diaspora has settled, including Delhi, Mumbai, and abroad.

 

NOTE

 

• Madai Festival (Option 1): A tribal festival of Chhattisgarh, marking the harvest season and worship of village deities.

 

• Vishwakarma Puja (Option 3): Dedicated to Vishwakarma, the divine architect/craftsman, celebrated mainly by artisans and factory workers.

 

• Sorath Sabha (Option 4): Not a recognised Sun-worship festival; the term is unrelated to Usha/Surya worship.

question: Which of the following inscriptions of Rudradaman happened to be the first royal inscription of early India composed in chaste Sanskrit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Girnar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Girnar (Junagadh) rock inscription of Rudradaman I, dated to around 150 CE, is the first known royal inscription of early India composed entirely in chaste/classical Sanskrit (prose). (गिरनार शिलालेख — रुद्रदामन)

 

• Rudradaman I was a ruler of the Western Kshatrapa (Saka) dynasty, and the inscription records his repair of the Sudarshana Lake, originally built during the Mauryan period.

 

• Before this, most royal inscriptions (like Ashoka's) were in Prakrit; the Girnar inscription marks a major shift towards Sanskrit as the language of royal epigraphy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Girnar hill in Junagadh, Gujarat, also bears the fourteen Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka and a later inscription of Skandagupta, making it a layered epigraphical site.

 

• The Sudarshana Lake inscription tradition shows continuous royal patronage — from Chandragupta Maurya to Ashoka to Rudradaman to Skandagupta.

 

NOTE

 

• Prayag (Option 1): Site of the Allahabad Pillar (Prayag Prashasti) inscription of Samudragupta, composed by Harishena, later than Rudradaman's Girnar inscription.

 

• Chirand (Option 3): A Neolithic-Chalcolithic archaeological site in Bihar, not associated with Rudradaman's inscriptions.

 

• Mehrauli (Option 4): Site of the Iron Pillar inscription (Delhi), attributed to a Gupta-era king (usually identified as Chandragupta II), unrelated to Rudradaman.

question: The first southern campaign of Alauddin Khilji in 1307-08 AD was led to which of the following regions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Devagiri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alauddin Khilji's first southern campaign (1307-08 AD) was directed against Devagiri, ruled by the Yadava king Ramachandradeva, and was led by his general Malik Kafur. (देवगिरी अभियान — अलाउद्दीन खिलजी)

 

• Devagiri had earlier been raided by Alauddin himself in 1296, but this 1307-08 campaign was specifically to punish Ramachandradeva for withholding tribute.

 

• Ramachandradeva was defeated and later reinstated as a loyal tributary, and Devagiri became a base for Malik Kafur's subsequent southern expeditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Malik Kafur's later campaigns targeted Warangal (Kakatiyas, 1310), Dwarasamudra (Hoysalas, 1311), and Madurai (Pandyas, 1311) — in that order, after the Devagiri campaign.

 

• Alauddin Khilji's southern campaigns marked the first major Delhi Sultanate expansion into peninsular India.

 

NOTE

 

• Warangal (Option 2): Capital of the Kakatiya dynasty, attacked by Malik Kafur in 1310, after the Devagiri campaign.

 

• Dwar Samudra (Option 3): Capital of the Hoysala dynasty, attacked by Malik Kafur in 1311.

 

• Madura (Option 4): Capital of the Pandya dynasty, the final target of Malik Kafur's southern campaigns in 1311.

question: What is the IUPAC name of tertiarybutyl alcohol?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2-Methylpropan-2-ol.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tertiary-butyl alcohol (tert-butanol), with formula (CH₃)₃C-OH, has the IUPAC name 2-Methylpropan-2-ol. (टर्शियरी ब्यूटाइल अल्कोहल — 2-मेथिलप्रोपेन-2-ऑल)

 

• In IUPAC nomenclature, the longest carbon chain containing the -OH group is a propane (3-carbon) chain, numbered so that the hydroxyl group gets the lowest possible locant (C-2), with a methyl substituent also at C-2.

 

• It is a tertiary alcohol because the carbon bearing the -OH group is attached to three other carbon atoms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• tert-Butanol is used as a solvent, denaturant for ethanol, and octane booster/oxygenate in gasoline, and as an intermediate to produce MTBE.

 

• The other butanol isomers are n-butanol (butan-1-ol), sec-butanol (butan-2-ol), and isobutanol (2-methylpropan-1-ol).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2, 3, 4: These names are not chemically valid/consistent IUPAC names for any butanol isomer — a propane chain cannot bear substituents at position 3 while numbering from position 1 for the -OH at position 1 in the way described; they are distractors with incorrect locants/structure.

question: What is the relationship between interest rate and demand for money?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Inverse.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to Keynes' Liquidity Preference Theory, the demand for money (especially speculative demand) and the rate of interest share an inverse (negative) relationship. (ब्याज दर और मुद्रा की मांग — प्रतिलोम संबंध)

 

• When the interest rate rises, holding money becomes costlier (higher opportunity cost, as interest-bearing assets become more attractive), so people demand less money and prefer to hold bonds/interest-bearing assets instead.

 

• Conversely, when the interest rate falls, the opportunity cost of holding money declines, so the demand for money rises.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Keynes identified three motives for holding money: transactionary, precautionary, and speculative; the inverse relationship with interest rate is most associated with the speculative motive.

 

• This inverse relationship underlies the downward-sloping LM curve in the IS-LM macroeconomic model.

 

NOTE

 

• No relationship exists (Option 1): Incorrect — a well-established inverse relationship exists, central to monetary theory.

 

• Direct (Option 3): Incorrect — this is the opposite of the actual relationship.

 

• Proportionate (Option 4): Incorrect — the relationship is inverse, not a direct/proportionate one.

question: When electricity is passed through water, what kind of chemical reaction occurs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Decomposition.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Passing an electric current through water (electrolysis) breaks it down into its constituent elements: 2H₂O(l) → 2H₂(g) + O₂(g). This is an example of a decomposition reaction, specifically electrolytic decomposition. (जल का विद्युत अपघटन — अपघटन अभिक्रिया)

 

• In a decomposition reaction, a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances, often requiring an external form of energy (heat, light, or electricity).

 

• During electrolysis of water, hydrogen gas is liberated at the cathode and oxygen gas at the anode, in a 2:1 volume ratio.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other types of decomposition include thermal decomposition (e.g., heating CaCO₃ to give CaO and CO₂) and photodecomposition (e.g., AgCl breaking down in sunlight).

 

• Electrolysis of water requires a small amount of electrolyte (like dilute H₂SO₄ or NaOH) to be added, as pure water is a poor conductor.

 

NOTE

 

• Displacement (Option 2): A reaction where a more reactive element displaces a less reactive one from its compound; not applicable here since water is broken into elements, not one element replacing another.

 

• Double displacement (Option 3): Involves an exchange of ions between two compounds; not applicable to a single-compound breakdown.

 

• Combination (Option 4): Involves two or more substances combining to form one product, the opposite of what happens during electrolysis of water.

question: Which music-composer duo was honoured with the National Lata Mangeshkar Award for the year 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anand-Milind.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The music-composer duo Anand-Milind was honoured with the National (Rashtriya) Lata Mangeshkar Award for the year 2020, conferred by the Government of Madhya Pradesh. (राष्ट्रीय लता मंगेशकर पुरस्कार — आनंद-मिलिंद)

 

• The Rashtriya Lata Mangeshkar Alankaran/Samman is given annually by the MP government to honour outstanding contributions to Indian music, in memory of legendary singer Lata Mangeshkar.

 

• In the same felicitation round (held after a pandemic-related backlog), Shailendra Singh was honoured for 2019 and Kumar Sanu for 2021.

 

• Anand-Milind, sons of veteran music director Anandji (of Kalyanji-Anandji), are known for composing music for films like Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The award carries a citation, memento, and a cash prize of ₹1 lakh, and is one of several state honours instituted by Madhya Pradesh in the field of arts.

 

• Madhya Pradesh also confers similar honours in other cultural fields, such as the Kalidas Samman for performing and visual arts.

 

NOTE

 

• Sachin-Jigar (Option 1): A contemporary Bollywood/Gujarati music-composer duo, not the 2020 National Lata Mangeshkar awardees.

 

• Jatin-Lalit (Option 2): A well-known 1990s Bollywood composer duo, not honoured with this specific 2020 award.

 

• Salim-Sulaiman (Option 3): A contemporary composer duo known for background scores and songs, not the 2020 awardees.

question: Which of the following can be represented as a functional unit of nature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ecosystem.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An ecosystem is considered the basic functional unit of nature/ecology, as it comprises a community of living organisms (biotic components) interacting with their non-living environment (abiotic components) as a self-sustaining system. (पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र — प्रकृति की क्रियात्मक इकाई)

 

• Within an ecosystem, energy flow (via food chains/webs) and nutrient cycling (via biogeochemical cycles) take place, making it "functional" rather than just structural.

 

• The term "ecosystem" was coined by A.G. Tansley in 1935.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ecosystems are broadly classified as terrestrial (forest, grassland, desert) and aquatic (freshwater, marine).

 

• Components of an ecosystem include producers, consumers (primary, secondary, tertiary), and decomposers.

 

NOTE

 

• Vehicles (Option 1): A man-made object, not a natural functional unit.

 

• Humans (Option 3): A single species/biotic component, not a complete functional unit by itself.

 

• Plants (Option 4): Only the producer component of an ecosystem, not the complete functional unit.

question: In which state of India is Kund or Tanka used for water harvesting?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kund (or Tanka) is a traditional underground covered rainwater harvesting tank used in the arid regions of Rajasthan, especially in the Thar Desert (Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Barmer regions). (कुंड/टांका — राजस्थान)

 

• A kund typically has a saucer-shaped catchment area that slopes towards a central circular underground storage tank, designed to collect and store scarce rainwater for drinking purposes.

 

• These structures were essential for survival in a region with very low and erratic rainfall, where groundwater is often saline or too deep to access.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other traditional Rajasthani water-harvesting structures include Baoris/Bawaris (stepwells), Nadis (village ponds), and Khadins (agricultural runoff-harvesting systems).

 

• Similar traditional harvesting systems elsewhere in India include Ahar-Pyne (Bihar), Zabo (Nagaland), and Eri (Tamil Nadu).

 

NOTE

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 2): Traditionally uses systems like Cheruvu (tanks), not Kund/Tanka.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Not traditionally associated with Kund/Tanka water harvesting.

 

• Punjab (Option 4): A relatively water-abundant state (Indus river system), not traditionally associated with Kund/Tanka structures.

question: The inaugural match of the Women Premier League 2023 cricket was played in which of the following venues?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The inaugural match of the Women's Premier League (WPL) 2023 was played on 4 March 2023 at the Brabourne Stadium, Mumbai, between Mumbai Indians and Gujarat Giants. (महिला प्रीमियर लीग 2023 — मुंबई)

 

• Mumbai Indians won this opening match, and they went on to win the inaugural WPL title (2023) as well, defeating Delhi Capitals in the final.

 

• The WPL is the BCCI-run T20 franchise league for women's cricket in India, launched in 2023, on the lines of the men's IPL.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The five inaugural WPL franchises were Mumbai Indians, Delhi Capitals, Gujarat Giants, UP Warriorz, and Royal Challengers Bangalore.

 

• Smriti Mandhana (RCB) was the leading run-scorer and Amelia Kerr was among the standout performers of the inaugural WPL 2023 season.

 

NOTE

 

• Delhi (Option 1): Hosted the WPL 2023 final, not the inaugural (opening) match.

 

• Chennai (Option 3): Not a venue for the WPL 2023 opening match.

 

• Kolkata (Option 4): Not a venue for the WPL 2023 opening match.

question: Which of the following is NOT correct about Directive Principles of State Policy?
option_1: They ensure social and economic development.
option_3: They provide guidelines for the governance of the country.
option_4: They are morally binding on the government.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They are justiciable in nature.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs), given in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution, are non-justiciable — meaning they cannot be enforced by any court of law. (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व — गैर-न्यायोचित/non-justiciable)

 

• Despite being non-justiciable, DPSPs are "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Article 37) and it is the duty of the State to apply these principles while making laws.

 

• They aim to establish a welfare state by promoting social and economic democracy, guiding the government toward goals like reducing inequality, ensuring a living wage, and promoting international peace.

 

• The concept was borrowed from the Irish Constitution, which in turn borrowed it from the Spanish Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• DPSPs are often contrasted with Fundamental Rights (Part III), which ARE justiciable and enforceable in court.

 

• Landmark cases like Kesavananda Bharati (1973) and the 42nd Amendment (1976) clarified and tried to balance the relationship between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs.

 

NOTE

 

• They ensure social and economic development (Option 1): This is a correct statement about DPSPs' purpose, hence not the answer.

 

• They provide guidelines for the governance of the country (Option 3): Correct — Article 37 explicitly calls them "fundamental in the governance of the country", hence not the answer.

 

• They are morally binding on the government (Option 4): Correct — though not legally enforceable, they carry moral and political weight, hence not the answer.

question: At what latitude does the easterly jet stream blow over peninsular India during the summer months?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14°N.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tropical Easterly Jet Stream (TEJ) blows over peninsular India, roughly along 14°N latitude, at an altitude of about 14-16 km, during the summer monsoon months (June-September). (पूर्वी जेट स्ट्रीम — 14°N अक्षांश)

 

• It flows from east to west, originating over the Indo-China Peninsula/South China Sea region, crossing southern India and extending across the Arabian Sea to Africa.

 

• The TEJ is closely linked to the onset and strength of the Indian summer monsoon — its presence is considered essential for a normal monsoon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The easterly jet is distinct from the subtropical westerly jet stream, which blows over northern India (around 25°-30°N) mainly in winter and steers western disturbances.

 

• The withdrawal of the westerly jet from north of the Himalayas in early summer is one of the triggers for monsoon onset over India.

 

NOTE

 

• 24°N, 30°N, 28°N (Options 1, 2, 4): These latitudes are associated with the subtropical westerly jet stream's winter position over northern India, not the summer tropical easterly jet over the peninsula.

question: According to Census of India 2011, in rural India, which state has the maximum female workforce participation rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, Himachal Pradesh recorded the highest female work(force) participation rate in rural India, reflecting the state's traditionally high involvement of women in agriculture and allied activities. (हिमाचल प्रदेश — ग्रामीण महिला कार्यबल भागीदारी दर)

 

• Work Participation Rate (WPR) is defined as the percentage of total workers (main + marginal) to the total population.

 

• Hilly and predominantly agrarian states like Himachal Pradesh tend to show higher female WPR because women are extensively engaged in farm and livestock-related work, which the census counts as economic activity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Northeastern states (e.g., Sikkim, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh) also tend to show relatively high female work participation rates compared to the national average.

 

• At the all-India level, the female work participation rate as per Census 2011 was around 25.5%, much lower than the male rate.

 

NOTE

 

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 1): Has a relatively high female WPR among northeastern states, but not the highest as per Census 2011.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 2): Has one of the lowest female work participation rates among Indian states.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Has a moderately high female WPR but ranks below Himachal Pradesh as per Census 2011 data.

question: In 2021, in which of the following states did the Prime Minister lay the foundation stone for the Raja Mahendra Pratap Singh State University?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone of the Raja Mahendra Pratap Singh State University at Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, on 14 September 2021. (राजा महेंद्र प्रताप सिंह राज्य विश्वविद्यालय — अलीगढ़, उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• The university is named after Raja Mahendra Pratap Singh, a freedom fighter, social reformer and educationist who founded the first President of the Provisional Government of India (formed in Kabul, 1915) and also established the Prem Mahavidyalaya at Vrindavan.

 

• The university is set up to promote higher education, especially technical and skill-based education, in the Aligarh region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Raja Mahendra Pratap Singh contested the first Lok Sabha election (1952) from Mathura as an independent candidate and won.

 

• The event in 2021 was part of a series of university/institution foundation-stone-laying programmes by the PM across Uttar Pradesh ahead of state elections.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Nagaland (Options 2, 3, 4): The Raja Mahendra Pratap Singh State University is located in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, not in any of these states.

question: When was a Madrasa opened in Kolkata to promote the study of Arabic, Persian and Islamic law?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1781 C.E.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Calcutta Madrasa (Madrasa Aliah) was established in 1781 by Governor-General Warren Hastings to promote the study of Arabic, Persian, and Islamic law (Muslim personal law), chiefly to train Indians to help administer Muslim law in British courts. (कलकत्ता मदरसा — वारेन हेस्टिंग्स, 1781)

 

• It reflected the early colonial Orientalist policy, under which the British initially supported the study of classical Indian and Islamic learning.

 

• The Madrasa is regarded as one of the oldest institutions of Islamic/Oriental learning set up under British rule in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In a similar vein, the Sanskrit College at Benares (Varanasi) was established in 1791 by Jonathan Duncan to promote the study of Hindu law and philosophy.

 

• Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal (1772-1785), and is also associated with the Regulating Act of 1773 and the impeachment trial that followed his return to Britain.

 

NOTE

 

• 1772 C.E. (Option 1): The year Warren Hastings became Governor of Bengal, not the founding year of the Calcutta Madrasa.

 

• 1783 C.E. (Option 2): Not the correct founding year of the Calcutta Madrasa.

 

• 1774 C.E. (Option 4): The year the Regulating Act came into effect and the Supreme Court at Calcutta was established, not the Madrasa's founding year.

question: Which Article of the Constitution explains that the executive power of every state shall be so exercised as not to impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union, and the executive power of the union shall extend to the giving of such directions to a state as may appear to the Government of India to be necessary for that purpose?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 257.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 257 of the Constitution states that the executive power of every State must be exercised so as not to impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union, and empowers the Union to give directions to a State as necessary for that purpose. (अनुच्छेद 257 — संघ और राज्यों के बीच कार्यपालिका शक्ति)

 

• Article 257 falls under Part XI (Relations between the Union and the States), specifically dealing with administrative relations.

 

• Under this Article, the Union can also direct States on matters like construction/maintenance of means of communication of national/military importance and protection of railways.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 256 similarly obliges States to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament and empowers the Union to give directions for that purpose.

 

• Non-compliance with directions under Articles 256/257 can be treated as a ground for imposition of President's Rule under Article 356.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 261 (Option 1): Deals with "full faith and credit" to be given throughout India to public acts, records, and judicial proceedings of the Union and States.

 

• Article 247 (Option 2): Empowers Parliament to establish additional courts for the better administration of laws made by it.

 

• Article 123 (Option 4): Empowers the President to promulgate Ordinances when Parliament is not in session.

question: Which of the following statements correctly defines the green revolution?
option_1: It is a new strategy in agriculture to produce food grains, especially wheat and rice.
option_2: It is a new strategy to increase the share of the forest.
option_3: It is a new strategy to use green colour for all purposes.
option_4: It is a new strategy to use only herbal products.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is a new strategy in agriculture to produce food grains, especially wheat and rice.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution refers to the dramatic increase in food grain production, especially wheat and rice, in India from the mid-1960s onward, achieved through High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilisers, pesticides, and assured irrigation. (हरित क्रांति — खाद्यान्न उत्पादन में वृद्धि)

 

• It was pioneered in India largely due to the efforts of agricultural scientist M.S. Swaminathan, often called the "Father of the Green Revolution in India", along with Norman Borlaug globally.

 

• The revolution was concentrated mainly in states with assured irrigation, notably Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India achieved self-sufficiency in food grains as a direct result of the Green Revolution, moving away from dependence on imports (like under PL-480).

 

• Criticisms of the Green Revolution include regional disparities, over-exploitation of groundwater, and soil degradation due to excessive chemical fertiliser use.

 

NOTE

 

• Increase the share of forest (Option 2): This describes goals related to afforestation/forest policy, not the Green Revolution.

 

• Use green colour for all purposes (Option 3): Not a real or meaningful definition; a distractor.

 

• Use only herbal products (Option 4): Unrelated to the Green Revolution, which in fact promoted chemical fertilisers and pesticides.

question: In the year 1952, who among the following lent his voice for the film ‘Amar Bhupali’, which was being produced in two languages simultaneously and he sang in both Bengali and Marathi ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manna Dey.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1952, Manna Dey lent his voice for the film 'Amar Bhupali' (Amar Bhoopali), which was produced simultaneously in two languages — Bengali and Marathi — and he sang for both language versions. (अमर भूपाली — मन्ना डे)

 

• This assignment helped establish Manna Dey as a top-ranking playback singer in Bengali cinema, in addition to his growing reputation in Hindi films.

 

• The film 'Amar Bhoopali' (based on the life of the Marathi poet Honaji Bala) was originally a V. Shantaram production, with music composed by Vasant Desai.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manna Dey was one of the most versatile playback singers of Hindi cinema, known for classical-based songs like "Ae Mere Pyare Watan" and "Pooche Jo Koi", and was honoured with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (2007).

 

• He was fluent in singing across multiple Indian languages, including Bengali, Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, and others.

 

NOTE

 

• Kishore Kumar (Option 1): A leading Hindi/Bengali playback singer of that era, but not the singer associated with the bilingual 'Amar Bhupali' assignment described.

 

• Hemanta Mukherjee (Hemant Kumar) (Option 2): A well-known Bengali/Hindi playback singer and music director, but not associated with this specific 'Amar Bhupali' bilingual role.

 

• Debabrata Biswas (Option 3): A renowned exponent of Rabindra Sangeet, not associated with playback singing for 'Amar Bhupali'.

question: In which part of India does the hot wind ‘Loo’ blow?
solution_text:
The correct answer is North and Northwestern.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Loo' is a strong, hot, dry wind that blows over the North and Northwestern plains of India (such as Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, and parts of Madhya Pradesh) during the summer months (especially May-June). (लू — उत्तर और उत्तर-पश्चिम भारत)

 

• It typically blows from the west or northwest towards the east, during the afternoon hours, and can cause heatstroke and even death if exposure is prolonged.

 

• The Loo occurs due to intense surface heating over the north Indian plains just before the onset of the monsoon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Local people in the Loo-affected regions traditionally cover their heads/faces with cloth and avoid stepping out during peak afternoon hours to protect themselves.

 

• The Loo is often followed by pre-monsoon showers ('mango showers') in some parts, providing temporary relief before the monsoon fully sets in.

 

NOTE

 

• West and Southwestern (Option 1): Not the region typically associated with the Loo; western coastal areas are moderated by sea influence.

 

• East and Northeastern (Option 3): These regions experience more humid conditions and are not characteristically associated with the Loo.

 

• South and Southwestern (Option 4): Southern India, being peninsular and closer to the sea, has a more moderate climate and does not experience the Loo.

question: The government of which of the following states created a draft policy in 2022 for senior citizens on the basis of article 41, which aims to form a directorate for the welfare of senior citizens?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of Tamil Nadu released the Draft Tamil Nadu State Policy on Senior Citizens, 2022, grounded in Article 41 of the Constitution (a Directive Principle directing the State to make provisions for public assistance in cases of old age), and it proposes setting up a dedicated Directorate for the Welfare of Senior Citizens. (तमिलनाडु वरिष्ठ नागरिक नीति 2022 — अनुच्छेद 41)

 

• The policy was framed recognising Tamil Nadu's rapid demographic transition, with the state having one of the highest proportions of elderly population among Indian states.

 

• It covers areas like healthcare, financial security, social security, and elder-friendly infrastructure for senior citizens.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 41 of the Constitution (a Directive Principle of State Policy) directs the State to make effective provision for securing the right to public assistance in cases of old age, sickness, and disablement, within the limits of its economic capacity.

 

• The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 is the central legislation providing for maintenance and welfare of senior citizens across India.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka, Telangana, Kerala (Options 1, 2, 4): These states have their own welfare measures for senior citizens, but the specific 2022 draft policy based on Article 41 proposing a dedicated directorate was created by Tamil Nadu, not these states.

question: When was the High Court and Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Amendment Bill, 2021 introduced in Lok Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 30 November 2021.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The High Court and Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Amendment Bill, 2021 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 30 November 2021 by the Union Law Minister Kiren Rijiju. (न्यायाधीश वेतन संशोधन विधेयक — 30 नवंबर 2021)

 

• The Bill sought to amend two laws — the High Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Act, 1954 and the Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Act, 1958 — to revise pension and gratuity provisions for judges.

 

• It was passed by both Houses of Parliament during the Winter Session, 2021.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Bill provided for enhanced pension for judges who have served as acting Chief Justice or additional judges, ensuring greater parity in retirement benefits.

 

• Salaries and pensions of higher judiciary judges in India are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and do not require annual parliamentary vote.

 

NOTE

 

• 27 September 2021, 29 March 2021, 28 April 2021 (Options 1, 3, 4): These are not the actual date of introduction of the Bill in Lok Sabha; the Bill was introduced on 30 November 2021.

question: At which Olympics did Gagan Narang win a bronze medal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is London 2012.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gagan Narang won the bronze medal in the Men's 10m Air Rifle shooting event at the London 2012 Olympics. (गगन नारंग — लंदन ओलंपिक 2012, कांस्य पदक)

 

• This was one of India's medals in the London 2012 Olympics, which was India's most successful Olympics at that time with a total of six medals.

 

• Gagan Narang is a decorated Indian shooter, also a recipient of the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna and Padma Shri.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Indian medallists at London 2012 included Vijay Kumar and Gagan Narang (shooting), Sushil Kumar and Yogeshwar Dutt (wrestling), Saina Nehwal (badminton), and Mary Kom (boxing).

 

• Gagan Narang later served as a member of various sports bodies and was involved in athlete mentorship after retirement from competitive shooting.

 

NOTE

 

• Rio 2016 (Option 2): Gagan Narang did not win a medal at the Rio Olympics.

 

• Athens 2004 (Option 3): Gagan Narang competed but did not win an Olympic medal at Athens.

 

• Beijing 2008 (Option 4): Gagan Narang did not win a medal at the Beijing Olympics (he narrowly missed a medal in the 10m air rifle event).
